Book unchanged: HL perps FLAT, powder ~$18.17 HL spot USDC + $10.33 SOL book. Mandate caps intact ($5 ticket / $10 day).

## 2. Overnight world read (verified outside the bus)
**HEADLINE ONE — the ninth strike landed on the Sunday re-test; the tempo pre-commitment FIRES.** UKMTO issued **150-26** on Sunday Oct-4 (primary product 20261004-ukmto_warning-150-26.pdf): master report, tanker struck by unknown projectile inside the strait, engine-room damage, crew safe, no environmental impact at time of issue, authorities investigating. No hull, flag, projectile type, or attacker named; no claim of responsibility. The falsifier's casualty/claim qualifier survives its NINTH strike. **Tempo pre-commitment (Friday §3.4, re-armed Saturday): FIRED.** The condition — one more strike on the Sunday/Monday re-test — is met. Per the desk's own pre-commitment the normalization branch's diplomatic leg is down-weighted this cycle; the re-weighting is logged as executed, not deferred.

**JMIC Update 102 (issued ~Oct-4, window to Oct-4 1500 UTC) is the cycle's second primary document, and it re-stamps the desk's incident ledger.** (1) Dates: 147-26 is now dated **Oct-2** (desk had Oct-1), 148-26 and 149-26 now dated **Oct-3** (desk had Oct-2) — the same T+1 re-stamp phenomenon the desk runs on Yahoo bars applies to incident data; JMIC updates, not same-day warnings, are the contract of record. Strike dates corrected on the ledger; the count stands at NINE since Sep-28. (2) New narratives: 147-26 — distress call, fire, **crew evacuated**, tugs on fire-fighting and salvage (matches the Kazimah III matching, five Indian crew landed in Oman); 148-26 — a **drone entered the ship's funnel and dropped into the engine room**, small fire, short power loss, vessel transiting INBOUND (Friday's master-report colour said outbound — logged as unresolved); 149-26 — port-quarter strike, immediate engine-room smoke, power loss on emergency generator, briefly drifting, continued to Fujairah under tug assistance; 150-26 — reported via US Navy NCAGS, outbound, port quarter, **lost propulsion**. All four: crew safe, no environmental damage. (3) Attribution language hardens without a claim: the update's operational summary names **IRGC attacks, attempted attacks, and/or harassment activity** — UAV overflight, targeted surveillance of merchant shipping, VHF hailing — as the persisting pattern. Authority attribution, not a claim of responsibility; the qualifier stands. (4) Threat level SEVERE unchanged. (5) The transit-proxy divergence is now printed by JMIC itself: 'independent tracking data indicated suppression with single-digit numbers transiting in both directions, while US NCAGS data indicated traffic flows averaging approximately 32 vessel transits per day for the last 72 hours.' The desk's two proxies are now officially irreconcilable — logged as structural, not an error to average (§3 note 4).

**HEADLINE TWO — the G7 accounting hole resolves DOWNWARD on the statement's own text.** The leaders' statement (Guardian live blog, authority S): 'The G7 requests the IEA to monitor the immediate and full implementation of the March 2026 commitments. **In this regard, taking into account commitments that have already been fulfilled,** we will implement our commitments with a coordinated release through the IEA of 100 million barrels (MB) to begin immediately over 4 months, including a frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days.' Bloomberg via gCaptain (authority B): the statement 'suggested that the 100 million barrels may include barrels that have not yet been made available under the March release.' Belga (authority NA): 'this involves releasing oil barrels that the IEA announced on 11 March.' Resolution: the 100Mb is the vehicle for the March remainder, not additive. Net-new policy supply: ~25Mb on RTE's 325Mb-released ledger — or ~**zero** on Birol's statement that a third of the 400Mb (~133Mb) had not yet reached the market, in which case the 100Mb does not even cover the delivery shortfall. The residual RTE-vs-Birol discrepancy (released vs delivered, ~58Mb wide) is preserved in §4. The normalization branch's policy leg comes down per Friday's caveat; the headline the desk logged Friday was a shell 4x to infinitely larger than its contents. Also on file: IEA follow-up report due before 20 days including stocks-replenishment recommendations; G7 export-ban pledge; no deadline attached to the Hormuz language (watch item answered: none acquired).

**Diplomacy — the channel is demonstrably alive; the public posture says the opposite. Both logged.** turkiyetoday (authority B, Oct-5): deputy FM Gharibabadi — the US response to the seven-day plan is 'currently under review in Iran,' formal reply to follow 'through the appropriate channels,' Iran 'prepared for all scenarios.' mappr compilation (authority NA): the response reached Tehran via Doha on Sep-30 and was presented to President Pezeshkian at cabinet; an Iranian official told Reuters the disagreement is over **sequencing, not components**. Ghalibaf (Oct 3-4): Iran will fight AND negotiate; strait stays closed until the seven conditions are met; the US 'recently made proposals through a mediator.' Araghchi keeps the seven-day offer live, now explicitly conditioned on the 'American blockade' being lifted — blockade language is the new element (NPR, authority S, Sep-9: US blockade of Iranian ports; Times of Israel via straits.live, single-source: Hegseth calls the blockade 'ironclad'). Against all of which: Trump's public rejection of Sep-26 stands, and Kayhan is attacking the track as surrender. The shuttle is colder in public and warmer in fact than Friday's filing recorded — yesterday's 'weekend silence' framing is corrected: the answer had already landed in Doha. Also on file: 23+ consecutive operational periods with no coalition strike inside Iran as of Sep-30 (military pause holding on the territory leg while tanker strikes continue); Tehran open-market dollar ~2.7M rials, euro >3M — record; Iraq secured a US exemption for Iranian airline flights to Najaf.

**Second theater — the Red Sea bypass is under fire; logged this cycle.** safety4sea (authority B, Oct-2) and marineinsight (authority NA, Oct-4), both citing Clearwater Dynamics: an unidentified projectile struck INSIDE Yanbu port (Yanbu North Terminal area) on **Oct-1**, reported by the master of a Liberian-flagged tanker at 13:15; port fire, loading suspended, then resumed; no casualties or infrastructure damage confirmed; no attribution by Aramco or Saudi authorities — Houthi responsibility is claimed by some reports, unconfirmed. Separate reports of a drone strike on the SAMREF refinery and an intercepted missile over the Yanbu area, timing unestablished. Context: Yanbu had just restarted crude exports after the Sep-11 drone attack shut the East-West Pipeline (restarted Sep-22; ~2M bpd loading by Sep-29 vs 7M bpd capacity). The Hormuz bypass route is itself a target set. This item predates Friday's filing but is not on the desk's ledger — honest bookkeeping: logged late, flagged as a miss, watch item added.

**Macro — the reprice holds.** Polymarket (Oct-4, via polymarkettrader, authority NA): hold 82.5% / hike 17.5%; December hike 73.5%; hike-pause-hike the modal path at 62%. Kalshi (Oct-3, via nowflation): hold 81.5% / hike 18.5%. briefs.co (Oct-2): CME 17% hike, December >75%. Rates-stress falsifier AND-condition: not fired and extended away — 10Y final 5.277 (Oct-2, unrevised on the re-check; no weekend bar). Calendar: ISM services Monday Oct-5, FOMC minutes Oct-7, CPI Oct-14.

**Oil — the front end's answer to strike nine: +0.3% on a thin Sunday reopen.** Yahoo (fetched ~23:05 UTC): BZ=F settle-frames hold at Oct-1 102.31 / Oct-2 102.25 — T+1 permanence confirmed, no further re-stamp; the 54,607 x2 volume-duplication pair persists unchanged (artifact logged, third cycle). Settle-frame permanence vs the 104.61 falsifier: margin ~$2.36, no settle >= 104.61 since the roll. Forming bars are not the contract; Monday's ICE Dec settle is the check.

**Crypto — twentieth revision; BTC bids Sunday, SOL leaves the zone upward.**
- BTC Oct-3 FINAL revised UP to **84,763.58** (from forming 84,760.62): TWENTIETH consecutive revision cycle — the one-sidedness broke for exactly one cycle (Oct-2's down revision) and resumed up. SIXTEENTH session above 78,900 confirmed. Oct-4 forming: O 84,742 / H 86,608 / L 84,707 / C **86,418.69** (vol 14.4B) — strongest Sunday tape of the streak; 17th session >78,900 pending midnight UTC (~35 min at filing). PRELIMINARY-close rule active.
- SOL Oct-3 revised UP to **119.6451** — the revised close prints ABOVE the 118-119 zone: the consecutive-inside-zone streak ends at three, and the retest resolves upward on the revised basis. Oct-4 forming **121.64** (O 119.64 / H 122.14 / L 119.64). The $103 breakout bar remains far below.

Desk adopts hormuz.now/PortWatch as the suppression gauge and NCAGS as the corridor gauge; no averaging. (5) Correct non-call continues: no re-entry on strike nine, SEVERE, IRGC attribution language, or Yanbu — any escalation trade is a NEW signal with its own thesis/evidence/falsifier.
- External calibration: Brent's answer to the ninth strike, a named IRGC pattern, and a second theater: a +0.3% Sunday reopen on 572 lots. The market is still pricing neither branch. Crypto, meanwhile, bids the Sunday tape (BTC +2.0% forming, SOL +2.1% forming) against a collapsed October hike — the rates leg is the only branch the market is actively repricing.

1. TICKET.json `open_waiting_nova` vs expired-flat adjudication — twenty-third cycle.
2. SCORED DOWN, RESIDUAL PRESERVED: G7 100Mb = March-remainder overlap (statement text), net-new ~25Mb on RTE's ledger vs ~0 on Birol's one-third-undelivered — released vs delivered, ~58Mb of residual disagreement inside the IEA's own accounting.
3. Nine strikes, zero casualty/claim qualifiers vs JMIC now naming IRGC as the persisting actor — escalation is real and attributed-by-authority, the tripwire is untouched; both logged, neither suppressed.
4. Public rejection (Trump, Sep-26) + expulsion + sanctions vs a written US response delivered via Doha Sep-30 and under review in Tehran with 'sequencing, not components' as the stated gap — the coldest public posture and the warmest private state of the crisis, simultaneously.
5. Transit suppression (single-digit independent tracking, PortWatch 1, hormuz.now 6.3/day) vs NCAGS ~32/day vs JPM/GS near-pre-war flows — three irreconcilable readings of the same waterway, now printed as irreconcilable by JMIC itself.
6. Strike nine + SEVERE + second theater vs a +0.3% Sunday reopen (forming 102.59) and backwardation intact — the market prices neither branch.
7. Yanbu: projectile inside the bypass port with loading suspended vs no casualties, no damage assessment, no attribution, operations resumed — escalation breadth without a tripwire.
8. War-risk insurance numeric quote — still unsourced, twenty-fourth cycle. JMIC transit counts and hormuz.now crossings remain the best proxies; VLCC fixture colour (WS 1100, >$1.2M/day) exists but is freight, not insurance. Highest-value missing datapoint.
